title: Soft-rule breaks: how often, not only whether
eyebrow: judge measure · soft rules · recomputed from saved test traces · 2026-11-20
subtitle: The judge counted a broken soft rule once per episode, however often it broke. It now also counts each separate break. On saved test traces, ARM-FM broke "try not to drop the key" about 220 times per episode where the old count said 0.79, and on the zombie garden the new count tells warm-started runs (about 10 breaks) from plain PPO (about 16), which the old count ranked the other way.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text: A soft rule is a "try not to" rule: breaking it is allowed, but a good agent breaks it rarely. Pass or fail counts only the goal and the hard rules, so soft rules need their own quality number. The old number said whether each soft rule broke at least once in an episode. An agent that drops the key once and one that drops it 200 times scored the same. The judge now also counts separate breaks: one break lasts while the rule's labels stay as they were on the break step, and the rule starts again when they change. Pass or fail is unchanged. All numbers below are recomputed from test traces saved by earlier runs, with no new training.

items.label: ARM-FM on cx-goal-one-rule: soft rules broken per episode (old) to separate breaks per episode (new)
FARM experiments on the two BlockedUnlockPickup cards with 0 separate soft breaks (the other: the ablation with no soft-break charge, 0.97)
zombie garden rerun, separate breaks: plain PPO vs warm-started (old count 1.14 vs 1.36: the other way round)
experiments where the recomputed old count differs from the stored one

items: **ARM-FM's machine pays for the drop.** On cx-goal-one-rule the ARM-FM agent picks up the key and drops it every other step, from about step 10 to the end of each 576-step episode, and never opens the door: 23,653 separate `key_lost` breaks in 100 test episodes of seed 1. Its machine paid it 25.2 per episode for that while the task was never done (live re-judge below).

**Zero breaks is not care by itself.** cx-goal-one-rule is judged 0 in every arm, FARM included: an agent that never finishes may simply never hold the key long enough to drop it. The FARM rows that do reach the goal on cx-goal-many-rules (judged 0.66 to 1.0) also show 0 breaks.

**Some rules never break.** Existence, ExistenceTwo, Response and RespondedExistence can only stay open at the end, so they add nothing to the count (they show as `soft_open`). On cx-goal-many-rules only Absence(key_lost) can break; Response(has_door_key, door_open) stays open.

**The forcing lanes number needs care.** On the forcing suite FARM has 1.05 separate breaks against 10.58 for no-RM, but FARM breaks the hard top-lane rule in every episode, which ends the game near step 80. Its machine (main, before `deff802`) charges a hard break less than a stream of soft breaks; the pay-order check still flags it, and it is generated again at the freeze.

sections.title: How a break is counted
sections.intro: `_break_count` in `app/src/benchmark/declare_judge.py`: judge the trace; on a break, count one and start the rule again from the first later step whose labels differ from the break step's. A label true on several steps in a row is one break.

rows: each new run of b before any a
each run of a trigger with no response
each time the pair comes back together
never: these can only stay open at the end

blocks.text: The NotCoExistence row is the record's own example: the pair is together from step 2 on; after the break the rule restarts at step 3, where a never comes true again, so b on step 4 is not a new break. Every example count in this table was computed with `_break_count` itself.

sections.title: Recomputed on saved test traces
sections.intro: Greedy test episodes of each experiment's seeds (100 per seed), judged again with the new code. Old: soft rules broken per episode, as stored in each judge.json. New: separate breaks per episode, and the share of episodes with at least one.

rows: chain regression ok2, ok4, ok5, reworded

items: **Zombie garden.** Every `lt-*` run trained the same machine (`graphs/lanes-rules-tune.rm`). Judged success counts only the hard top lane, so it reads 0.91 to 1.0 everywhere. The old count saw every episode break at least one of the two soft rules (1.1 to 1.36 of them on average) and ranked the warm starts worse. The new count puts the four warm-started runs of the zombie-garden entry (R5-bcft, R5d-bcft12, R6-cont, WS-warm) at 10.2 to 10.5 and every other `lt-*` run at 14.5 to 16.8, in line with that entry's side-breach count (17.15 to 9.85).

**What this does not show.** The zombie-garden warm start is a hack (a behaviour clone of a hand-written policy) and still tramples too many plants; fewer breaks here is a measurement result, not a learning result.

items.text: Worktree and experiment as saved. Episodes is the total over the experiment's seeds (100 greedy test episodes per seed; dry runs have fewer).

sections.title: Live re-judge with the new judge
sections.intro: The suite table run with the new code on finished seed-1 runs, no training (`aggregate-suite` on a suite file cut to one card): the ARM-FM cx-goal-one-rule run, and the forcing lanes-rules runs, which had never been judged. The new columns appear beside the old ones. One seed, so the table compares behaviour only and gives no verdict.

blocks.text: On ta1 both hard clauses were never activated (Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) and Existence(target_picked_up) at 0.00): the agent never opened the door. The forcing FARM line is the kept pay-order flag at work: hard break -1 against soft break -47.5 on that machine ([kept-flags.out in the pay-order entry](../pay-order-started/evidence/kept-flags.out)).
